subject: ClearThera follow-up: exactly what Redwood stores for prompts & outputs
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lena Park <lena.park@clearthera.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: ClearThera follow-up: exactly what Redwood stores for prompts & outputs

Hi Lena — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our call and the items you asked us to confirm about PII/prompt-output handling: 

1) Default hosted behavior: we do not persist customer prompt/response text by default in a way that is searchable or used for model training. For teams on the hosted API, we keep ephemeral request-context in memory to serve the call and the KV cache; the raw request/response payloads are retained in short-term logs for debugging/ops (default 7 days) unless you opt into extended logging.

2) Audit/logging options: for troubleshooting and SLO reasons we offer an opt-in logging tier (enterprise) that retains an encrypted copy of request/response pairs for up to 90 days. These logs are scoped to the customer and stored in the logical region you choose (us-west, eu-west).

3) Dedicated / Private: if you run on Dedicated or Private deployments under a contract, you control retention via the deployment config — Redwood does not ingest or index prompt/output content for training. By default dedicated pools do not forward logs to the hosted analytics cluster.

4) Residency & encryption: data at rest is encrypted with customer-managed KMS on Private; for Hosted we use provider KMS with per-tenant encryption keys. Residency options: US (us-west/us-east) or EU (eu-west) for enterprise tenants; logs are kept in-region unless you authorize cross-region replication.

5) PII redaction & telemetry: we offer a pre-processing hook (client-side library or server-side filter) to mask or strip fields before sending to the API. We also provide a small SDK sample that hashes IDs and strips PHI fields.

I attached a short PDF that summarizes these options and a snapshot of the SOC2 evidence page we referenced on the call. Can you confirm the two things you asked for: (A) whether ClearThera needs prompt/response storage disabled entirely, or just restricted to the 7-day default; and (B) which residency region you want us to propose in the PO (us-west or eu-west)?

Proposed next steps: I can provision a short trial in the us-west region with logging disabled (no stored request/response) and a scope-limited debug window for your SREs. If you prefer, we can also prepare a DPA + configuration addendum that locks retention to 7 days.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 20-min tech call with your security engineer if that helps.

— Aditya
Aditya Rao
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
aditya@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0148

From: Lena Park <lena.park@clearthera.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: security@clearthera.com
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 15:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: ClearThera follow-up: exactly what Redwood stores for prompts & outputs

Hi Aditya — thanks for the detailed recap. A few clarifying questions for our InfoSec/Comms checklist: 

• When you say "short-term logs for debugging (default 7 days)", is that full plaintext of prompt and model output, or are sensitive fields redacted by default?

• For the enterprise opt-in 90-day logs: is there a per-field access control (e.g., SRE can see request IDs but not PII unless they explicitly request unredacted copies)? We want a principle of least privilege.

• If ClearThera wants "no storage at all" (strict ephemeral), what is the impact on debugging and support? Will Redwood still be able to provide token-level billing and latency metrics?

• For residency: we will need data to be in the US (us-west) for the PoC. Does the trial you mentioned default to US?

We want a short written statement we can include in our procurement packet that says: "Redwood does not retain or use prompt/response text for model training and will only retain stored copies per the negotiated retention period" — can you provide that language to include in the PO?

Also please include the name of the KMS approach for hosted vs private so our InfoSec folks can validate with the cloud team.

— Lena Park
Product & Security Liaison, ClearThera
lena.park@clearthera.com

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lena Park <lena.park@clearthera.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: ClearThera follow-up: exactly what Redwood stores for prompts & outputs

Lena — answers inline below.

• Plaintext in 7-day logs: yes, the 7-day debug logs contain full request/response payloads in plaintext so that we can reproduce and debug. We understand that is sensitive; that's why we offer the SDK filter and the ability to disable logging altogether for the trial.

• Access controls on 90-day enterprise logs: logs are encrypted at rest and access is role-based. By default, SREs can see metadata (request IDs, timestamps, latency, model variant). Unredacted payload access is gated: a support engineer must request unredacted access and it requires a documented justification and an approval step in our ticketing workflow. We can include that process in the DPA.

• Impact of strict ephemeral (no storage): debugging becomes more constrained to real-time tracing and metrics (latency, token counts, error rates). We can provide token-level billing and high-level traces (sampled) without storing full payloads. For deep reproduction of a bug that depends on prompt content you would need to re-run a request or opt into a temporary debug window (time-limited, audit-logged).

• Trial region: I will provision the trial in us-west by default per your request. It will be configured with logging disabled and telemetry-only metrics preserved (no stored request/response).

Requested PO language (suggested):

"Redwood Inference confirms that it will not use customer prompt or model output text for model training. Prompt and response payloads are only retained as described in the service configuration: default hosted debug logs (7 days) unless the customer elects to disable storage, and an opt-in enterprise logging tier (up to 90 days). For Dedicated and Private deployments, retention is controlled by the customer's deployment configuration. All stored copies are encrypted at rest and access-controlled per Redwood's documented procedures."

KMS details: Hosted: provider-managed KMS keys with per-tenant key wrapping; Private/Dedicated: supports customer-managed KMS via AWS KMS (CMKs) or Google Cloud KMS. We will include the KMS key identifiers in the DPA annex for the PO.

I attached the short summary and SOC image. If that language looks good I can add it to the proposed PO and send a one-page DPA addendum for signature.

Next step: I'll spin up the us-west trial later today and share credentials for your SREs to validate. Can Marissa help with the DPA addendum?

— Aditya

Attachments: redwood-prompt-output-data-handling-summary.pdf
